claim: Db2, MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL DB instances can have up to 64 TiB of storage, and every DB instance has a primary storage volume with a maximum capacity of 64 TiB.
question: What is the maximum storage of an RDS for MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL or Db2 DB instance?

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance (Db2, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL); per primary storage volume for every engine
qualifiers.condition: most DB instance classes; some smaller or previous-generation classes have lower maximums

evidence.quote: Every DB instance has a primary storage volume with a maximum capacity of 64 TiB.
You can create Db2, MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL RDS DB instances with up to 64 tebibytes (TiB) of storage.

claim: RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server DB instances can have up to 256 TiB of storage by adding additional storage volumes; each additional volume holds up to 64 TiB.
question: What is the maximum storage of an RDS for Oracle or SQL Server DB instance that uses additional storage volumes?

values.spoken: up to sixty-four tebibytes per additional volume

qualifiers.condition: only with additional storage volumes

evidence.quote: You can create Oracle and SQL Server instances with up to 256 TiB of storage with additional storage volumes.
Each additional volume allocates up to 64 TiB of storage, up to a maximum of 256 TiB per instance.

note: The brief says this changed on 2025-11-14; the current page states 256 TiB but no old value, so no changed object is set here (decisions+changes lens).

claim: With RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server you can attach up to three additional storage volumes to a DB instance, each gp3 or io2.
question: How many additional storage volumes can an RDS for Oracle or SQL Server DB instance have?

values.display: up to three additional storage volumes
values.spoken: up to three additional storage volumes

qualifiers.condition: storage autoscaling isn't supported for additional storage volumes

evidence.quote: With RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server, you can attach up to three additional storage volumes to your DB instance.

claim: A manual increase of a storage volume must be at least 10%, and allocated space can't be deallocated.
question: What is the smallest manual storage increase for an RDS DB instance, and can storage be reduced?

evidence.quote: You can increase the allocated space on a storage volume by a minimum of 10%.
You can't deallocate space.

claim: Storage autoscaling starts a storage increase when free available space is less than or equal to 10 percent of the allocated storage (together with the other trigger conditions).
question: At what free-space level does RDS storage autoscaling start a storage increase?

values.spoken: ten percent of the allocated storage

qualifiers.condition: the low-storage condition must also last at least five minutes, and the previous modification must have finished optimizing

evidence.quote: Free available space is less than or equal to 10 percent of the allocated storage.

claim: Storage autoscaling acts only when the low-storage condition lasts at least five minutes.
question: How long must the low-storage condition last before RDS storage autoscaling acts?

qualifiers.condition: one of three trigger conditions

evidence.quote: The low-storage condition lasts at least five minutes.

claim: Storage modifications are limited to a maximum of four within any 24-hour period, and a further modification can't start until storage optimization of the previous one completes.
question: How many storage modifications can an RDS DB instance have in 24 hours?

values.display: a maximum of four modifications within any 24-hour period
values.spoken: at most four storage modifications in any twenty-four hours

qualifiers.condition: applies to storage autoscaling too: it acts only when fewer than four storage modifications occurred in the past 24 hours

evidence.quote: This is because further storage modifications can't be made until storage optimization completes on the instance, and are limited to a maximum of four modifications within any 24-hour period.
Storage optimization has completed on the instance for the previous storage modification, and fewer than four storage modifications have occurred in the past 24 hours.

note: What's New 2026-07-15 announced up to four storage modifications in 24 hours; the old rule (the brief's hypothesis: once per six hours) is not stated on this page. A launch on 2026-07-15 sits on the 'not examinable yet' boundary of RULINGS rule 7; older exam questions may assume the six-hour wait.

claim: The maximum storage threshold for storage autoscaling must be at least 10% more than the current allocated storage; AWS recommends at least 26% more to avoid an event notification.
question: How far above the allocated storage must the RDS maximum storage threshold be set?

evidence.quote: You must set the maximum storage threshold to at least 10% more than the current allocated storage.
We recommend setting it to at least 26% more to avoid receiving an [event notification](USER_Events.Messages.md#RDS-EVENT-0225) that the storage size is approaching the maximum storage threshold.

claim: The default maximum storage threshold for storage autoscaling is 1,000 GiB, so with the default an instance doesn't autoscale above 1,000 GiB.
question: What is the default maximum storage threshold for RDS storage autoscaling?

qualifiers.condition: you can set a higher threshold up to the maximum allocated storage of the engine and instance class

evidence.quote: The default maximum storage threshold for autoscaling is 1,000 GiB.
If you use this default, the instance doesn't autoscale above 1,000 GiB.

claim: Enabling storage autoscaling doesn't require a database reboot and doesn't cause any downtime.
question: Does turning on RDS storage autoscaling cause downtime or a reboot?

evidence.quote: Enabling storage autoscaling doesn't require a database reboot and doesn't cause any downtime.

claim: Storage autoscaling can't decrease the allocated storage, and you can't reduce the storage of a DB instance after it has been allocated.
question: Can RDS storage autoscaling or a modification reduce allocated storage?

values.display: Autoscaling can't decrease the allocated storage

qualifiers.condition: to shrink, use a blue/green deployment or a new DB instance with less storage

evidence.quote: Autoscaling can't decrease the allocated storage.
You can't reduce the amount of storage for a DB instance after storage has been allocated.

claim: AWS recommends io2 Block Express storage for I/O-intensive, latency-sensitive workloads, with up to 256,000 I/O operations per second.
question: What is the maximum IOPS of RDS io2 Block Express storage?

values.display: up to 256,000 I/O operations per second
values.spoken: up to two hundred fifty-six thousand IOPS

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance storage (io2 Block Express)
qualifiers.condition: the DB instance class can impose a lower limit

evidence.quote: For I/O-intensive and latency-sensitive workloads, we recommend that you use Provisioned IOPS SSD io2 Block Express storage to achieve up to 256,000 I/O operations per second (IOPS).

claim: For io2 Block Express, the ratio of IOPS to allocated storage (in GiB) must be from 0.5–1,000; for DB instances not based on the AWS Nitro System it must be from 0.5–500.
question: What IOPS-to-storage ratio does RDS io2 Block Express storage allow?

values.spoken: from half to one thousand IOPS per gibibyte
from half to five hundred IOPS per gibibyte

qualifiers.condition: with storage autoscaling the same ratio applies to the maximum storage threshold

evidence.quote: The ratio of IOPS to allocated storage (in GiB) must be from 0.5–1,000.
For DB instances not based on the AWS Nitro System, the ratio must be from 0.5–500.

claim: On io2 Block Express, maximum IOPS can be provisioned with volumes of 256 GiB and larger (1,000 IOPS × 256 GiB = 256,000 IOPS).
question: From what volume size can RDS io2 Block Express storage reach its maximum IOPS?

values.spoken: two hundred fifty-six gibibytes and larger

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance (io2 Block Express, Nitro-based)
qualifiers.condition: for instances not based on the AWS Nitro System, maximum IOPS are reached at 512 GiB

evidence.quote: Maximum IOPS can be provisioned with volumes 256 GiB and larger (1,000 IOPS × 256 GiB = 256,000 IOPS).

claim: For io1 storage, the ratio of IOPS to allocated storage (in GiB) must be from 1–50 on RDS for SQL Server and 0.5–50 on the other RDS DB engines.
question: What IOPS-to-storage ratio does RDS io1 storage allow?

qualifiers.condition: io1 is the previous generation; AWS recommends io2 Block Express where available

evidence.quote: The ratio of IOPS to allocated storage (in GiB) must be from 1–50 on RDS for SQL Server, and 0.5–50 on other RDS DB engines.

claim: On gp3 storage volumes, Amazon RDS provides a baseline storage performance of 3000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s.
question: What baseline IOPS and throughput does RDS gp3 storage include?

values.spoken: one hundred twenty-five mebibytes per second

qualifiers.scope: per gp3 storage volume (below the striping threshold)
qualifiers.condition: for striped volumes the baseline is 12,000 IOPS and 500 MiB/s

evidence.quote: On gp3 storage volumes, Amazon RDS provides a baseline storage performance of 3000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s.

claim: For striped gp3 volumes (four volumes instead of one, above a storage-size threshold; not on RDS for SQL Server), Amazon RDS provides a baseline of 12,000 IOPS and 500 MiB/s.
question: What baseline performance does RDS gp3 storage give once the volume is striped?

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance with striped gp3 storage
qualifiers.condition: every engine except RDS for SQL Server, which doesn't support volume striping

evidence.quote: For striped volumes, Amazon RDS provides a baseline storage performance of 12,000 IOPS and 500 MiB/s.
This is because of *volume striping*, where the storage uses four volumes instead of one.
RDS for SQL Server doesn't support volume striping, and therefore doesn't have a threshold value.

claim: On gp3, the maximum ratio of IOPS to allocated storage is 500 and the maximum ratio of storage throughput to IOPS is 0.25, for all supported DB engines.
question: What ratio limits apply to provisioned IOPS and throughput on RDS gp3 storage?

qualifiers.condition: on RDS for SQL Server the minimum IOPS-to-storage ratio is 0.5

evidence.quote: The maximum ratio of IOPS to allocated storage is 500 for all supported DB engines.
The maximum ratio of storage throughput to IOPS is 0.25 for all supported DB engines.

claim: gp2 storage has a baseline I/O performance of 3 IOPS for each GiB, with a minimum of 100 IOPS, so larger volumes perform better.
question: How is the baseline IOPS of RDS gp2 storage calculated?

qualifiers.condition: gp2 is the previous generation; IOPS can't be provisioned directly on gp2

evidence.quote: Baseline I/O performance for gp2 storage is 3 IOPS for each GiB, with a minimum of 100 IOPS.

claim: Individual gp2 volumes below 1,000 GiB can burst to 3,000 IOPS for extended periods, limited by the volume's I/O credit balance.
question: Up to what IOPS can a small RDS gp2 volume burst?

qualifiers.condition: burst performance depends on the I/O credit balance

evidence.quote: Individual gp2 volumes below 1,000 GiB in size also have the ability to burst to 3,000 IOPS for extended periods of time.
Volume I/O credit balance determines burst performance.

claim: Magnetic storage is deprecated and no longer offered for new DB instances, and starting July 1, 2026, you can no longer restore a snapshot to magnetic storage.
question: Can you still create or restore RDS DB instances on magnetic storage?

values.display: no longer offered for new DB instances
values.spoken: no longer offered for new DB instances

qualifiers.condition: existing magnetic volumes were migrated to gp3

evidence.quote: Magnetic storage is deprecated and is no longer offered for new DB instances.
Starting July 1, 2026, you can no longer restore a snapshot to magnetic storage.

note: Older exam questions may still offer magnetic storage as a low-cost option.

claim: A dedicated log volume (DLV) is supported only for Provisioned IOPS storage (io1 and io2 Block Express) and is created with a fixed size of 1,024 GiB and 3,000 Provisioned IOPS.
question: What size and IOPS does an RDS dedicated log volume have?

qualifiers.condition: DLVs aren't supported for gp2 and gp3

evidence.quote: DLVs are supported for PIOPS storage (io1 and io2 Block Express), and are created with a fixed size of 1,024 GiB and 3,000 Provisioned IOPS.

claim: All RDS for SQL Server DB instances, apart from io2 Block Express storage, have a maximum storage of 16 TiB.
question: What is the maximum storage of an RDS for SQL Server DB instance that doesn't use io2 Block Express?

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance (SQL Server, storage types other than io2 Block Express)
qualifiers.condition: the gp3 table on the same page lists 20–65,536 GiB for SQL Server; record both, see note

evidence.quote: All RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instances apart from io2 Block Express storage have a maximum storage of 16 TiB, so there are no entries for SQL Server.

note: The same page is not consistent: the gp3 table lists SQL Server at 20–65,536 GiB, the comparison table lists gp3 and gp2 with 16,384 GiB on SQL Server, and the instance-class section says 16 TiB apart from io2 Block Express. Writers should cite the table row they use.

claim: With Provisioned IOPS storage, you are charged for the provisioned resources whether or not you use them in a given month.
question: Do you pay for provisioned IOPS on RDS when you don't use them?

values.display: whether or not you use them
values.spoken: whether or not you use them

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance with Provisioned IOPS storage

evidence.quote: With Provisioned IOPS storage, you are charged for the provisioned resources whether or not you use them in a given month.
